rules.statement: When serializing an ML-DSA (AKP) private key to a JWK, write `priv` as the 32-byte seed only, never the expanded private key, and write `pub` as the raw public key.
rules.why: RFC 9964 defines the AKP key representation as seed form only for `priv` and the raw public key for `pub`.
rules.check: Look for AKP/ML-DSA JWK export or import code that writes or accepts the expanded private key in `priv`, or that puts anything other than the raw public key in `pub`.

rules.statement: Store asymmetric key material at rest as standard PKCS#8 (private) or SubjectPublicKeyInfo (public) DER, including post-quantum key types, instead of a raw or custom format.
rules.why: Every asymmetric family then has the same at-rest format, the parameter set is self-describing through its OID, and X.509 interop stays possible.
rules.check: Look for a new asymmetric key type that persists or deserializes its key material as raw bytes, a seed blob or a custom encoding instead of PKCS#8/SPKI DER.

rules.statement: Suppress an `[Experimental]` BCL diagnostic (such as SYSLIB5006) with a narrowly scoped `#pragma warning disable` at the specific call site, plus a comment pointing to the decision that justifies it, and never suppress it project-wide.
rules.why: Narrow suppressions keep the reliance on experimental APIs visible, and they can be deleted with no other change once the BCL drops the flag.
rules.check: Look for experimental diagnostic IDs disabled in .csproj, Directory.Build.props, .editorconfig or GlobalSuppressions, or for a pragma that spans more than the call sites that need it or has no justifying comment.

rules.statement: Gate platform-dependent signing algorithms on their runtime support check (for example `MLDsa.IsSupported`) so that discovery metadata and JWKS never advertise an `alg` the running OS cannot sign or verify.
rules.why: Advertising an algorithm the platform cannot fulfill is an interop bug.
rules.check: Look for algorithm registrations or data sources that add OS-dependent algorithms (ML-DSA and similar) to the advertised set without checking the primitive's IsSupported property.

rules.statement: Make tests that exercise OS-dependent cryptographic primitives no-op when the primitive's IsSupported check is false, so they don't fail on CI platforms without support.
rules.why: This keeps the tests portable across CI operating systems.
rules.check: Look for tests that use MLDsa or other OS-dependent crypto types without first checking IsSupported, so they would throw PlatformNotSupportedException on some CI runners.

rules.statement: Make a catalog `internal` when a specification fixes it to a closed set (such as the three FIPS 204 ML-DSA parameter sets), and let callers select an entry by its `alg` name instead of extending the catalog.
rules.why: The spec defines exactly those entries and each one is its own `alg`, so a public extension point would have no valid use.
rules.check: Look for a new public or consumer-extensible catalog or registry whose entries a specification fixes.

rules.statement: Implement a cryptographic algorithm by composing the stable in-box BCL primitive when one exists, and don't add a third-party cryptographic dependency or a custom implementation for it.
rules.why: A stable BCL primitive needs no third-party dependency and fits the same pattern as the existing RSA and ECC algorithms.
rules.check: Look for a new third-party crypto package reference, or hand-written crypto math, for an algorithm that System.Security.Cryptography already supports in a stable form.
